name: Split-foot malformation-mesoaxial polydactyly syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical diagnostic criteria for Split-foot malformation-mesoaxial polydactyly syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of split-foot malformation characterized by median cleft of the foot
Mesoaxial polydactyly involving duplication of central rays of the foot
Syndactyly or fusion of toes adjacent to the cleft
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of split-foot malformation with mesoaxial polydactyly confirmed clinically or radiographically
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory

common.symptomName: Symphalangism of the proximal phalanx of the 2nd toe with the 2nd metatarsal
Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the distal phalanx of the hallux
Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the phalanges of the 3rd toe
Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the phalanges of the 4th toe
Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the phalanges of the 5th toe
Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the distal phalanx of the 2nd toe

imaging: Radiographs showing median cleft of the foot with central ray duplication
X-ray evidence of syndactyly and hypoplastic foot rays
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic foot malformations

distinguishingFeatures: Typically involves both hands and feet
Polydactyly usually postaxial or preaxial rather than mesoaxial
Polydactyly located on ulnar or fibular side
Absence of median cleft in foot

redFlags: Severe foot deformity causing inability to ambulate
references: Orphanet: Split-foot malformation-mesoaxial polydactyly syndrome - ORPHA:488232
Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM) - Limb malformations
Tzschach et al., Clinical and genetic aspects of split-foot malformation, European Journal of Medical Genetics, 2020
